title: Ellington as compiler, not composer
summary: Ellington assembled the themes into Sophisticated Lady; Brown once called him a compiler and said the band was a cooperative in spirit but not in money.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Those eight bars that became "Sophisticated Lady" were originally a solo in another number, weren't they?

Well, they were not a solo -- it was just a thing you played. There are always a lot of pieces or a lot of footage we'll say that was just played along. It had no particular meaning, or wasn't meant to be a piece. It was just like a -- say an obligato against something, or even an exercise study. But you pick up everything, you know.
But you don't remember where they -- you first played them?
No.
In what song?

I think Otto used to play that as part of his. I can't remember what song it was, but he definitely had a tune that he used to play that theme in -- the release theme of "Sophisticated Lady". Then after they finally made "Sophisticated Lady" and got together, you know, and made about 50 different versions, and 50 different takeoffs, and 50 different performances of everybody and every way, and that's the way you make more and more.
What did Duke have to do with "Sophisticated Lady"?
Compiling.
It was his idea to put your eight bars first --
Right. Yeah.
-- and Otto's contribution in the middle, right?
Right. Yeah. In fact, this is one of the first times that we came near breaking up, because I told him that I don't consider you a composer. You are a compiler. To which his ego boiled over.
But yet he continued to that practice, did he not?
Oh, that's the basis of the operation.
I think that you were -- you had a thing that you made earlier about the band.

Yes, I told him that I think -- I didn't think there had ever been a band that should have been incorporated any more than this band. Everyman in there was a part of the music, the band, and everything that happened, and every successful move that the band made.
I think off the tape you -- you said it was really a cooperative.
It really was a cooperative in spirit, not in the money.
Not in --
Salary. Right.
